voci.titolo: Trillion-Dollar Dislocation Hides in Calm Credit Markets
voci.riassunto: Corporate credit has rarely looked calmer. Yet, underneath the surface, about $1 trillion of bonds are telling a different story.

voci.titolo: Sticky Inflation Is Roiling Bond Markets Again
voci.riassunto: Borrowing costs everywhere are heading higher.

voci.titolo: BlackRock’s Wei Li Prefers US Equities to Government Bonds
voci.riassunto: Wei Li, global chief investment strategist at BlackRock, says, “right now, from a total portfolio perspective,” she prefers equities over credit and government bonds, however she does see “good income opportunities within fixed income that we do want to lean into.” (Source: Bloomberg)

voci.titolo: Euro zone inflation is back above 3%. Higher interest rates are likely to follow
voci.riassunto: The European Central Bank is seen hiking rates in September as the Iran war raises energy costs in the region.

voci.titolo: Are rising bond rates really so bad? Maybe not, say these exports
voci.riassunto: The near-zero interest rates that characterized the decade after the global financil crisis were a sign of economic dysfunction. Higher rates reflect a stronger demand for capital and robust economic growth.

voci.titolo: From the U.K. to Japan, bond yields are jumping as U.S. bonds tumble
voci.riassunto: The old adage that the rest of the world sneezes when the U.S. catches a cold very much applies to bonds as well.

voci.titolo: US 30-Year Bond Enters September on Worst Stretch Since 2006
voci.riassunto: Not since 2006 have yields on the longest-maturity Treasuries been this high for this long, with a gaping budget deficit, another wave of corporate issuance and a potentially decisive Federal Reserve meeting set to keep investors wary of US debt in coming weeks.

voci.titolo: Gold Extends Drop as Fresh Mideast Tensions Raise Fed Hike Bets
voci.riassunto: Gold fell to the lowest in almost two weeks as fresh hostilities in the Middle East sent oil higher, adding to pressure on the Federal Reserve to lift interest rates.

voci.titolo: Bessent Ramps Up Pressure on BOJ to Raise Rates Further
voci.riassunto: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stepped up his increasingly public pressure on Japan to raise interest rates as the yen continued to weaken and the nation’s 10-year bond yield touched 3% for the first time since 1996.

voci.titolo: US Stocks Fall as Yields Climb on Rate Hike Bets: Markets Wrap
voci.riassunto: Stocks kicked off September on a weak note, with rising oil prices helping to push global bond yields higher and adding to bets that central banks will raise interest rates this month.

voci.titolo: Bank of England chief warns new AI models threaten global financial stability
voci.riassunto: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey has warned that frontier AI could materially increase cyber risks to the global financial system.

voci.titolo: India’s economy expands 7.8% in fiscal first quarter, beating estimates
voci.riassunto: The economy was driven by a strong performance in the financial, real estate, information technology and professional services sectors.

voci.titolo: China's factory activity shrinks for second straight month, contracting less than expected
voci.riassunto: China's manufacturing activity shrank for a second straight month, keeping pressure on Beijing to support the economy as growth loses momentum.

voci.titolo: Singapore tackles finances and culture to avert a demographic crisis
voci.riassunto: One challenge for policy makers is that success on many measures won't show up immediately.

voci.titolo: K, C or E? Why economists can’t agree on the shape of today’s economy
voci.riassunto: Economists have long viewed the post-pandemic economy as "K"-shaped. That consensus has now evaporated.

voci.titolo: Fed Chairman Warsh expresses concern about inflation, advocates for 'quieter' central bank
voci.riassunto: He used the speech to outline his philosophy on policymaking while carefully sidestepping any signals

voci.titolo: Fed's Hammack says 'now is the time to act' on raising interest rates
voci.riassunto: She still thinks the Fed needs to take action against inflation that is straining household budgets.

voci.titolo: Fed’s preferred inflation gauge shows core prices rose 3.3% annually in July
voci.riassunto: The personal consumption expenditures price index was expected to rise 0.1% monthly and 3.6% on a 12-month basis, according to economists surveyed by Dow Jones.
